literal: suffering experienced unable to bear wept tears are they not wealth wearing away weapon
translation: The tears wept by people unable to bear their suffering are the very weapon that will wear away the ruler's wealth.
modern: துன்பப்பட்டு அதனைத் தாங்க முடியாமல் மக்கள் அழுத கண்ணீர்தான் ஆட்சியாளரின் செல்வத்தை அழிக்கும் ஆயுதமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet warns an unjust ruler about the destructive power of the people's sorrow. When subjects are oppressed and weep because they cannot bear their suffering, their tears are not merely signs of grief. The poet metaphorically equates these tears to a powerful weapon that will gradually wear away and destroy the king's wealth and prosperity. It emphasizes that a ruler's true security lies in the happiness of the people, not in military might or accumulated riches.
